A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GNN-SSM research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial reformatting and additions.

before.justification: v1 reports original Cora, RingTransfer, graph-property prediction, and peptide experiments, together with spectral analyses and ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds runtime measurements, ogbn-arxiv and heterophilic evaluations, and further Cora ablations.

M1.justification: The GNN-SSM update, fixed shared state-space matrices, trainable coupling function, and k-hop extension remain unchanged. Equation 9's transposed notation and the newly disclosed construction of Λ do not establish an algorithm change. Trainable and unshared variants appear as ablations.

E1.justification: v2 retains the earlier datasets and adds ogbn-arxiv plus Amazon Ratings, Roman Empire, and Minesweeper (Appendices D.5 and D.7). These substantially broaden evaluation to a larger citation benchmark and additional heterophilic node-prediction settings.

E2.justification: GRED becomes an evaluated peptide comparator in Table 5; v1 only discussed its underlying work. Table 7 introduces comparisons involving NodeFormer, GOAT, EXPHORMER + GCN, and SPEXPHORMER. Comparator membership in the retained Tables 1, 2, and 4 is unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols include validation-selected depths of 4, 9, and 12 for the heterophilic tasks, AUC evaluation for Minesweeper, epoch-time measurements, an alternative feature-dispersion metric, and Cora controls extending to 256 layers. Table 3 also changes the peptide layer listing from 17,40 to 40,17, consistent with the existing prose; this does not establish rerunning earlier experiments.

E4.justification: v2 adds tests of shared versus unshared or trained Λ, Λ-spectrum changes versus tuning vanilla GCN weights, removal of B, and an alternative smoothing measure. Figure 4 adds GIN/Gated-GCN energy-divergence curves while reusing their earlier Jacobian histograms. The separate nonlinear GCN versus feedforward histogram from v1 Figure 7 is removed.

E5.justification: Appendix D.7 newly specifies averaging the heterophilic experiments over three random seeds. The existing four-initialization protocols and mean/standard-deviation reporting for graph-property and peptide experiments remain unchanged. The new disclosure does not indicate a change in runs for those earlier experiments.

E6.justification: All numerical results in Tables 1, 2, and 4 are retained. New results include GRED comparisons, runtime measurements, ogbn-arxiv accuracy of 72.49 ± 0.16, heterophilic outcomes, and matrix/spectral ablations. For example, new Table 11 reports 256-layer Cora accuracy of 13.0 without B versus 80.2 with B. These are additional results, not improvements to matched v1 scores.

T1.justification: The principal spectral and contraction results and Appendix A proofs are retained. Section 4 adds shared-versus-unshared fixed-point reasoning and an explicit convergence-rate statement in Lemma 4.1. The newly displayed rate O(1/L^n) grows rather than decays for 0 < L < 1, introducing a mathematical error.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction qualify extreme gradient vanishing as a problem of traditional GNNs and recast several claims around feature collapse and long-range modeling. The central contributions—connecting recurrent and graph learning, proposing GNN-SSM, and combining connectivity with non-dissipative dynamics—remain intact.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands the contraction-based interpretation to distinguish zero-feature collapse from instability and divergence in GIN/Gated-GCN. Appendix E explains B's damping role and the limitations of weight-spectrum tuning, and explicitly acknowledges that formal equivalence with the alternative smoothing measure is unproved. Appendix D.4 also clarifies the model's investigative purpose relative to GRED.

D1.justification: v2 newly describes constructing Λ by scaling a random unitary matrix, offers an eigendecomposition alternative, identifies a single NVIDIA RTX4090 GPU, and documents computational overhead and epoch times. These improve implementation and resource information without demonstrating changes to the retained method or experiments.

R1.justification: v2 adds substantive engagement with Arnaiz-Rodriguez and Errica's critique and Roth and Liebig's rank-collapse analysis, and details its differences from the already-cited GRED work. Appendix F expands positioning across deep, spectral, and temporal GNNs. References to coRNN and gradient gating are removed.

P1.justification: Section 4 is extensively rewritten and reordered around fixed points and feature collapse before discussing Dirichlet energy. Terminology changes throughout the abstract and introduction, explanatory Appendix E is added, and supplementary related work becomes Appendix F with the relocated limitations paragraph.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, with substantial resizing and repositioning of displays. Earlier Figures 2 and 3 are merged, selected appendix histograms move into main-text Figure 4, and seven tables plus a new smoothing-measure figure are added. Table 1 also gains an explicit MAE scale label.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the new matrix and spectral ablations better support the proposed design choices, while additional benchmarks and the GRED comparison broaden empirical scrutiny. The distinction between collapse and divergence also improves interpretation. These gains are tempered by sparse protocol details for some new evaluations and the incorrect convergence-rate expression introduced in Lemma 4.1, yielding a limited net improvement.
